#: the provenance. `stale_determinations` compares these.
STORED_ANSWER = ("state", "marker", "tier_basis", "derivation_sha", "rests_on_proxy_inference",
                 "regulatory_stratum_only", "code_floor_only", "value_min", "value_max",
                 "has_unverified_sources", "all_sources_disqualified")


def stale_determinations(conn):
    """The live determinations this engine wrote (`RULE_VERSION`) whose stored answer is no longer
    the one `determine` gives, as (specification_id, [the fields that differ]).

    THE STORED MARKER IS A CACHE. It is read off the sources' verification and tier, the rows'
    grading and comparators, and the `confirms` edges, and `derivation_sha` hashes none of them
    (K01 verifies only the stored junction, each figure's in-lens state read off the live lens links,
    and the conditioned governing claims, K02 only that the junction is complete). A lens link added
    to or retired from a figure moves that in-lens state, so it moves the sha and is reported here as
    `derivation_sha` (or as the lens, when no figure is stated in the cell's lens any more). The stored VALUE and its note are read off the `condition_on` edges
    from governing rows (`compose_value`): those edges are in the sha payload, so a filed or
    removed one makes the sha, and with it this check, differ. `db.py` refuses the
    routes it knows (a regrading, an edge, a source's engine-read columns); a data migration, the
    verification cron or a route not yet thought of does not pass through it. This is what
    notices, whichever route moved the input. The remedy is the one the refusals name: retire the
    specification, re-determine."""
    cols = ("specification_id", "parameter_id", *LENS_ORDER, *STORED_ANSWER)
    out = []
    for sid, pid, *rest in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT {', '.join(cols)} FROM specifications WHERE retired_at IS NULL "
            f"AND rule_version = ? ORDER BY specification_id", (RULE_VERSION,)).fetchall():
        lens = dict(zip(LENS_ORDER, rest))
        try:
            det = determine(conn, pid, lens, "", "recomputed")
        except Refusal:
            # The figures behind a stored cell can leave its lens when a link is retired.
            out.append((sid, ["lens (no figure is stated in it now)"]))
            continue
        diff = [f for f, was in zip(STORED_ANSWER, rest[len(LENS_ORDER):]) if det[f] != was]
        if diff:
            out.append((sid, diff))
    return out

def compose_value(conn, links, direction):
    """The determination's value from its HEADLINE claims; conditioned claims are branches (OR-2).

    A governing claim with an outgoing `condition_on` edge holds only under that condition
    (migration 075: "this figure only holds given a second figure"), so it is a branch beside the
    headline, never part of it (owner, OR-2: "Branches, and an empty headline when all are
    conditioned"). The edge points FROM the conditioned claim (`--from` the claim that holds only
    under the condition, `--to` the condition): an edge ARRIVING at a row conditions nothing (the
    relaxation rows point at the general claim they relax; reading them the other way would push the
    general claims out of the headline). Link roles are unchanged, so a conditioned row stays
    `governing`. Every note returned, a decline included, says how many claims are branches, and
    the notes of a headline that has branches name their denominator as UNCONDITIONED governing
    claims: a note computed over the headline alone is otherwise read as a statement about every
    governing claim. Returns what `_compose_headline` returns.

    OPEN OWNER QUESTION (OI-55 (9)): OR-2 (2026-10-29) puts a conditioned claim beside the headline
    even when it is the gentlest value; the rulings of 2026-10-30 say the gentlest value is the
    gentlest value and that the steepest code value is never highlighted. This function encodes
    OR-2 and does not reconcile the three."""
    conditioned = set(conditioned_governing(conn, links))
    headline = [l for l in links
                if not (l["role"] == "governing" and l["extraction_id"] in conditioned)]
    if conditioned and not any(l["role"] == "governing" for l in headline):
        return None, None, None, (f"piecewise only: all {len(conditioned)} governing claim(s) are "
                                  f"conditioned (condition_on); the branches are the answer"), None
    vmin, vmax, unit, note, notations = _compose_headline(
        conn, headline, direction, "unconditioned " if conditioned else "")
    if conditioned:
        note = ((note + "; ") if note else "") + (
            f"{len(conditioned)} conditioned claim(s) are branches, not the headline")
    return vmin, vmax, unit, note, notations

AFTER_DATA_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^--\s*AFTER_DATA:\s*(\d{14})\s*$", re.M)


def build_plan() -> list:
    """The faithful replay order, as a flat list of steps.

    Returns [("schema", version, path), ("data", ts, migration_id, path), ...].

    THE DEFAULT is what it has always been: every schema migration, then every
    data migration. That is right almost always, because schema precedes the
    data it shapes.

    IT IS WRONG WHENEVER A SCHEMA MIGRATION RENAMES OR DROPS SOMETHING THAT
    COMMITTED DATA MIGRATIONS STILL NAME. Data migrations are immutable, so they
    keep writing to the old name forever; a schema-phase rename runs first and
    they die on replay. Migration 025 hit this from the other side and had to
    withdraw a data migration to escape it. The 055 rename hit it from this side
    across 19 data migrations spanning two months, where withdrawal is not
    available.

    A numbered schema migration may therefore declare, on its own line:

        -- AFTER_DATA: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS

    meaning: this migration, and every migration numbered after it, applies only
    once the data migrations up to that timestamp have replayed. That is not a
    special case bolted on for one rename — it is the real chronology, which the
    numbered/timestamped split cannot otherwise express. Several markers may be
    present; each opens another data segment.
    """
    schema_migs = discover_schema_migrations()
    data_migs = discover_data_migrations()
    marks = []
    for i, (_v, path) in enumerate(schema_migs):
        m = AFTER_DATA_PATTERN.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if m:
            marks.append((i, m.group(1)))

    plan, si, di = [], 0, 0
    for idx, cutoff in marks:
        plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:idx]]
        si = idx
        while di < len(data_migs) and data_migs[di][0] <= cutoff:
            plan.append(("data",) + data_migs[di])
            di += 1
    plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:]]
    plan += [("data",) + d for d in data_migs[di:]]
    return plan

_One task, one pull request. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. ## 2. Preconditions

Until then it is the workplan branch, `origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0` (if that name is gone: `git branch -r --contains "$(git log --all --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md)"`). Check: `grep -F "OD-31 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1` must read `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`.

It holds item 3 and the engine change of item 3a, and through them this task: item 3 cannot be built without knowing which fact the column states, and items 1 and 2 retire `ALL` toward that same column. Check: `grep -F "OD-48 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1` must read `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`; then do item 3a's part for the answer given.
- **Tests that must be red (or green) before you start:** writers accept `ALL` as an identity, and the engine routes a figure tagged `ALL` to an `ALL` determination (OR-1b).

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

`ALL` is a scope marker filed as an identity, and it says what `specifications.design_scale = 'universal'` already says: two homes for one fact. The owner ruled that it leaves the identity lens. Today writers accept it, one of them refuses it only in a special case (`add-conflict`; `add-medical` was deleted on 2026-11-16 with the medical lens), and the engine's OR-1b predicate gives `ALL` figures their own determination.

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. **One retirement mechanism, a small variant of T-054.** `retire-identity` gains `--to-design-scale universal` as the alternative to `--need`: it marks the code `deprecated` and records that its successor is the determination's `design_scale`, with a typed column (for example `superseded_by_design_scale`, its value checked against the values `specifications.design_scale`'s CHECK declares, read with `dbcore.check_values`, never retyped), so the successor has one home and no prose. A CHECK keeps exactly one successor column set on a deprecated row. [2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] T-054 now adds two successor columns (`superseded_by_need`, `superseded_by_identity`) under one exactly-one CHECK; this task adds the third and widens that same CHECK, never a second rule. If T-054's shape makes a second column worse than a generalised successor, say so in the pull request and keep one home.
2. **Writers refuse `ALL` as an identity** once it is deprecated, by T-054's general refusal; the message names `design_scale = 'universal'` as where universality is stated, and, for a figure, the ICF and access-need lenses as where a provision that names no one is carried (OD-31). The special-case refusal in `scripts/db.py` (`add-conflict --pop-a/--pop-b ALL`) becomes that general refusal; delete the special case (`add-medical --identity ALL` went with the verb, 2026-11-16).
3. **The engine.** Remove the OR-1b predicate that routes `ALL` figures to an `ALL` determination; a determination of `design_scale = 'universal'` gathers by its ICF and needs lenses, never by an identity. Run the T-014 stress harness before and after; only the `ALL` paths may change.

Under OD-48 (a) "whom it is for": the G1 line sets `design_scale` from the key (`universal` when the determination has no identity code, `population` otherwise) and no longer from the stratum; "rests on codes only" is read from `regulatory_stratum_only` by every reader that read it from `design_scale` (sweep `design_scale` and `SCALE_UNIVERSAL`, section 5); `RULE_VERSION` is bumped by its derived rule. Under (b) "what it res
4. **No writer to move a figure's lens is built here** (corrected 2026-11-12 by `T-018-design.md` section 12). T-018 moves a figure's lens codes into `extraction_lens_links` and holds the figure's lens columns NULL, so a writer that rewrites `identity_code` on the figure would be deleted by the next task; and as first written it could not work, because `retire-identity` refuses a code that live rows still carry while this writer would move rows only off a code already `deprecated`. T-115 moves figures off `ALL` with T-018's `add-lens-link` and `retire-lens-link`, then retires `ALL` here. Do nothing for this item.
5. **Callers.** `governance/population-taxonomy.md` §1.3 (the `ALL` definition) gains one line that `ALL` has left the identity lens (OD-31) and universal is `design_scale`; the tests that use `ALL` (`git grep -l -E "['\"]ALL['\"]" -- scripts/tests`) are updated to the new refusal; skills naming `ALL` as a population are corrected. Change nothing else in governance.

**What reads what this task adds or changes:** every writer that takes an identity code; the engine; render (universal shown by `design_scale`); T-115.

**Code size.** Report `git diff --shortstat "$(git merge-base HEAD "$BASE")" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'`; this task should delete the two special cases and the OR-1b branch, so name what it deletes.

`basis_reason`, the recording session's judgment (OD-65; the sixteenth set of 2026-11-14,
                          as corrected 2026-11-15). Only on a source of tier 4 or above, the regulatory stratum: the
                          owner moved the assignment for code values only, so a research figure's group still comes
                          from its own words or its study's participants.

    `basis_reason` is given with `context` and with no other basis (a reason beside a stated warrant is a cell with no
    meaning). Returns (the stripped text, the stripped reason or None). WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHECK: that the words name
    the lens code itself. The registries
    do not hold a name for every code (about half the ICF d-codes have no title, access_needs has no name column), so a name test cannot be derived for them; whether the words name the group
    is the judge's (D-2) and the recorded warrant is what a later reader audits."""
    allowed = set(_lens_basis_choices() or ())
    if basis not in allowed:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: a lens link needs --lens-basis / --basis, one of {sorted(allowed)} (the warrant for "
            f"stating the figure in this group). Nothing was written.")
    reason = None if basis_reason is None else str(basis_reason).strip()
    if basis != "context" and reason is not None:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: a reason (--lens-basis-reason / --basis-reason) is the recording session's judgment and "
            f"belongs to basis `context` only; basis {basis} rests on the source's own words, so a reason beside it "
            f"would be a cell with no meaning. Nothing was written.")
    if basis == "context":
        tier = conn.execute("SELECT tier FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?", (ref_id,)).fetchone()
        if not (tier and tier[0] is not None and int(tier[0]) >= _REGULATORY_FROM_TIER):
            raise Refusal(
                f"{context}: basis `context` is for a code value (a source of tier 4 to 6); {ref_id} is tier "
                f"{tier[0] if tier else None}. The owner moved the contextual assignment of a lens to the recording "
                f"call for code values only (the sixteenth set, 2026-11-14: grep -n -F \"Owner instruction 2026-11-14 "
                f"(sixteenth set)\" references/project-standards.md); a research figure's group comes from its own "
                f"words (named_in_text, heading) or its study's participants. Nothing was written.")
        if not reason or not re.search(r"[^\W\d_]", reason):
            raise Refusal(
                f"{context}: basis `context` needs --lens-basis-reason / --basis-reason: your judgment, in words, "
                f"of why the clause's context warrants the link (for a mounting height: 'typically concerns "
                f"wheelchair users'). Nothing was written.")
    text = (basis_text or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant's words are blank. Give --lens-basis-text / --basis-text: the exact words "
            f"of the figure, its heading or its study's participants that name the group. Nothing was written.")
    if not re.search(r"\w", text):
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} holds no letter or digit, so it names no one. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")
    if basis == "named_in_text":
        where = f"the figure's claim_text, or a file saved for {ref_id}"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id)
    elif basis == "context":
        where = f"the figure's claim_text, its source_section, or a file saved for {ref_id}"
        found = (_as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _as_whole_words(text, source_section)
                 or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id))
    elif basis == "heading":
        where = "the figure's source_section (its heading)"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, source_section)
    else:
        where = f"the study_population of an evidence_population_match row for {ref_id}"
        found = any(_as_whole_words(text, r[0]) for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT study_population FROM evidence_population_match WHERE source_ref=?", (ref_id,)))
    if not found:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} (basis {basis}) is not, on word boundaries, in {where}. A link "
            f"rests on words the source holds, never on memory (CLAUDE.md 5(c)); a basis names where to look: "
            f"named_in_text the claim text or the source's saved file, heading the source_section, "
            f"study_participants the graded study_population, context the claim text, the source_section or the "
            f"source's saved file (its scope, application or purpose clause). Nothing was written.")
    return text, reason


def _refuse_all_by_context(basis, identity_codes, context):
    """`ALL` is not an identity (OD-31: "ALL leaves the identity lens"), so a judged context link never names it."""
    if basis == "context" and "ALL" in (identity_codes or ()):
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: --identity ALL by basis context: ALL is a scope marker, not a group (OD-31: grep -n -F "
            f"\"OD-31: a provision that names no one\" references/project-standards.md). Write the groups the clause "
            f"serves, or no identity. Nothing was written.")


def _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id: int, col: str, code: str, basis: str, basis_text, session: str,
                     basis_reason=None) -> int:
    """INSERT one live link and return its link_id. The caller has checked the code and the warrant."""
    row = {"extraction_id": extraction_id, col: code, "basis": basis, "basis_text": basis_text,
           "basis_reason": basis_reason, **dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "extraction_lens_links", session)}
    return conn.execute(
        f"INSERT INTO extraction_lens_links ({','.join(row)}) VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
        list(row.values())).lastrowid


# THE MAPS PROPOSE; THE RECORDING SESSION JUDGES (the correction of 2026-11-15: grep -n -F "Correction and registration
# 2026-11-15" references/project-standards.md). The identities `identity_icf_map` ties to a figure's ICF codes, and to
# the b/d codes `access_need_icf` gives its needs, are shown to the session before it writes, each with the map row's
# mechanism, confidence and provenance. Nothing is written because it was proposed, and nothing is refused because it
# was not: the proposals are reading for a judgment, never a lookup that decides (rule 8). One query, read by
# add-extraction, add-lens-link and scripts/audit/code_value_identity_audit.py.

def identity_proposals(conn, icf_codes, need_codes):
    """[dict] one per live map row proposing an identity for these ICF codes or needs: identity_code, icf_code,
    mechanism, mapping_confidence, provenance, via_needs (the given needs whose b/d row names that ICF code, or None),
    map_created_at and need_row_created_at (the newest such access_need_icf row, or None). A retired map row proposes
    nothing."""
    icf, needs = sorted(set(icf_codes or ())), sorted(set(need_codes or ()))
    if not icf and not needs:
        return []
    nm, im = ",".join("?" * len(needs)), ",".join("?" * len(icf))
    rows = conn.execute(
        f"SELECT m.identity_code, m.icf_code, m.mechanism, m.mapping_confidence, m.provenance, "
        f"  (SELECT group_concat(a.need_code) FROM access_need_icf a WHERE a.icf_code = m.icf_code "
        f"     AND a.icf_type <> 'e' AND a.need_code IN ({nm})), m.created_at, "
        f"  (SELECT MAX(a.created_at) FROM access_need_icf a WHERE a.icf_code = m.icf_code "
        f"     AND a.icf_type <> 'e' AND a.need_code IN ({nm})) "
        f"FROM identity_icf_map m "
        f"WHERE m.retired_at IS NULL "
        f"  AND (m.icf_code IN ({im}) OR m.icf_code IN (SELECT icf_code FROM access_need_icf "
        f"       WHERE need_code IN ({nm}) AND icf_type <> 'e')) "
        f"ORDER BY m.identity_code, m.icf_code, m.link_id", [*needs, *needs, *icf, *needs]).fetchall()
    keys = ("identity_code", "icf_code", "mechanism", "mapping_confidence", "provenance", "via_needs",
            "map_created_at", "need_row_created_at")
    return [dict(zip(keys, r)) for r in rows]

def add_lens_link(extraction_id: int, session: str, *, identity: str = None, icf: str = None,
                  needs: str = None, basis: str = None, basis_text: str = None,
                  basis_reason: str = None, dry_run: bool = False):
    """State an existing figure in ONE more lens code (OR-1c), with the words that warrant it.

    Refuses: a figure that does not exist; none or more than one code; a code the registry lacks or a
    retired identity (`_require_lens_code`); a missing basis, a blank or unfound warrant
    (`_require_lens_warrant`); a live link already holding the code, EXCEPT a `carried` one, which is
    retired in this same transaction ("superseded by judged link <id>") because a judged warrant
    replaces a carried one in one act. The retirement is written first and its reason completed once
    the new link has an id: the partial unique index admits one live link per (figure, code)."""
    given = {col: code for col, code in (("identity_code", identity), ("icf_code", icf),
                                         ("needs_code", needs))
             if code is not None}
    if len(given) != 1:
        raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: name exactly one code, with one of --identity / --icf / --needs "
                      f"(got {len(given)}). Repeat the verb for each code. Nothing was written.")
    ((col, code),) = given.items()
    if not isinstance(code, str):
        raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: {col} must be one code as text, got {code!r}. Nothing was written.")
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        fig = conn.execute(
            "SELECT ref_id, claim_text, source_section "
            "FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?", (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
        if fig is None:
            raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: extraction {extraction_id}: no such figure. Nothing was written.")
        _refuse_retired_figure(conn, extraction_id, "add-lens-link")
        _require_lens_code(conn, col, code)
        text, reason = _require_lens_warrant(conn, basis, basis_text, fig["ref_id"], fig["claim_text"],
                                             fig["source_section"], "add-lens-link", basis_reason=basis_reason)
        _refuse_all_by_context(basis, [code] if col == "identity_code" else [], "add-lens-link")
        held = conn.execute(
            f"SELECT link_id, basis FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE extraction_id=? AND {col}=? "
            f"AND retired_at IS NULL", (extraction_id, code)).fetchone()
        if held is not None and held["basis"] != "carried":
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-lens-link: extraction {extraction_id} already holds a live {held['basis']} link "
                f"({held['link_id']}) for {col} {code!r}. A figure holds one live link per code; retire it "
                f"first (retire-lens-link) if its warrant is wrong. Nothing was written.")
        # THE PROPOSALS (T-126), shown before the write: for the ICF codes and needs live on the figure and the one
        # being written.
        live = _live_lens_codes(conn, extraction_id)
        proposed = _print_identity_proposals(
            conn, live["icf_code"] + ([code] if col == "icf_code" else []),
            live["needs_code"] + ([code] if col == "needs_code" else []), "add-lens-link")
        if held is not None:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, retirement_reason=?, "
                "updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE link_id=?",
                [dbcore.now(), dbcore.session_stem(session), "superseded by judged link", dbcore.now(),
                 dbcore.session_stem(session), held["link_id"]])
        link_id = _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id, col, code, basis, text, session, basis_reason=reason)
        if held is not None:
            conn.execute("UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retirement_reason=? WHERE link_id=?",
                         (f"superseded by judged link {link_id}", held["link_id"]))
        _warn_identity_omitted(conn, extraction_id, fig["ref_id"])
        return {"link_id": link_id, "extraction_id": extraction_id, "lens": col, "code": code,
                "basis": basis, "retired_carried_link_id": held["link_id"] if held else None,
                "identities_proposed": proposed,
                "identities_written": _live_lens_codes(conn, extraction_id)["identity_code"],
                "dry_run": dry_run}


def retire_lens_link(link_id: int, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Retire one lens link in place (OD-29): the three retired_* columns and the updated_* pair.

    Refuses: no such link; already retired; a blank reason; and the figure's LAST live link, because a
    figure with no lens is a value about nobody (D-0182) and the schema no longer holds that rule."""
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        link = conn.execute("SELECT extraction_id, retired_at FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE link_id=?",
                            (link_id,)).fetchone()
        if link is None:
            raise Refusal(f"retire-lens-link: link {link_id}: no such link. Nothing was written.")
        if link["retired_at"] is not None:

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a live (not retired, migration 158) non-absent extraction exists for the pair
--                        (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only live claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- WHY THIS ORDER (it is derived from what each fact proves; 122 ranked BLOCKED above every
-- reading and 123 below every reading, both guesses): a FULL reading proves the obstacle
-- gone, since the whole text was read, so 3 outranks 4. A partial, fragment or abstract
-- reading proves nothing about the full text, so under a standing obstacle 4 outranks 5.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id
-- (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1
-- and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading
-- recorded; 3 wins over the rest because a full reading supersedes a partial one.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read", and
-- this header is the ONE HOME of the classification of every processing_blocked_reason
-- value (evidence_sources CHECK, migration 091); each value appears here as a bare token
-- under exactly one head, and a test derives the CHECK and fails on a value this header
-- does not name. The writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. NOTHING
-- CLEARS THE COLUMN: it is the retrieval record and stays as history; the ledger alone says
-- whether a pair is still blocked.
--   obstacle to the text (BLOCKED, above):  no-full-text, paywalled, language.
--   copy of a typed fact (not an obstacle; the writers refuse it by pointer -- the judgement
--     lives in db.py _BLOCK_REASON_COPIES): no-quantified-claims -> a recorded full reading;
--     superseded -> superseded_by_ref_id.
--   pending owner question 8 of the round-3 adjudication, treated as NULL (the source owes
--     its reading): out-of-scope, tier-not-required (they say no text was unobtainable);
--     no-doi, not-indexed (migration 091's comments describe discovery -- "no resolvable
--     identifier for automated paths", "absent from the indexes the pipeline queries" --
--     not an obstacle to a text in hand, and a URL-only report admitted without a DOI can
--     be read).
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent' AND x.retired_at IS NULL) THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent' AND x.retired_at IS NULL) THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id

scripts/audit/scan_debt.py — which (source, parameter) pairs nobody has read in full?

WHY THIS EXISTS (tooling T1, 2026-10-09; catalogue-plan-v2 sections 3.8 and 8.2). The
owner's requirement: "Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required
based on new information we come across." A parameter promoted in month three is owed a
look in month one's sources, and nothing showed that debt: the catalogue could imply "no
code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code for that quantity, while every gate
read green -- how GAP-061's figures were lost. `v_scan_ledger` (migration 103) derives a
status for every unsuperseded source x active parameter from the extractions and the
reading record (source_scans); this counts the pairs still owed.

DEBT = NOT-READ + READ-PARTIAL pairs. EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT and READ-NOTHING-FOUND are
accounted for. READ-PARTIAL is debt because a partial, fragment or abstract reading cannot
say a quantity is absent from the pages it did not see.

NO DEBT BASELINE, deliberately (the "no floor" this check was asked for). Debt RISES
legitimately -- every parameter promoted and every source admitted adds pairs -- so a
ratchet-down baseline would turn red on correct work. It is advisory and red whenever
debt > 0: the honest state of a catalogue that has not been read. Its readers: the next
cohort's worklist (the pairs printed below), the catalogue's evidence-state line, and the
Release 0 acceptance test (plan section 12, Q12), which will scope it to that source set.

EXAMINED is the number of ledger pairs. Zero pairs means no unsuperseded source or no
active parameter -- a corpus clear, which this project has done once (2026-09-13) -- and
the registry floor (min_items: 1) makes that visible rather than a silent pass.

THE RE-READ FLAG, `--reread` (T-031; OD-23, the owner 2026-11-12: "we can still read a source more than once--we
just want to minimize duplicate reads ... We can flag a source to be read again for later parameters"). Derived, never
stored, so it cannot drift from the scans. Only a source READ IN FULL (its latest `full` `full-read` reading) can be
read AGAIN; a pair of a source never read in full is plain debt. Each such owed pair takes the first route that reaches
it -- `inventory` (a clause recorded by the latest reading of the current file names the parameter: its v_term_names
display name or an attested form, v_attested_term_forms, matched word by word under retrieval_log.normalise_quote),
`retained-text` (the current file is on disk and still hashes to its sha256: sweep it), else `reread` (THE FLAG). The
matching rule is this module's: the task file states none (a design question for the owner); it is the narrowest
defensible one. A flag is cleared by recording the reading (record-scan --mode targeted, or catalogue). A judgment that
the inventory missed a clause is an open typed gap on the pair, not a second flag. Readers: this mode, and
`db.py cell-status` (evidence, owed, reread_flagged: a subset of never_examined and read_in_part_only).

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

A determination states a figure for disabled people in the units the sources used, converted exactly between them. ## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect. 1. **`add-unit`, by data, with a warrant (item 31).**
   - **Schema.** `base_units` gains `quote` (the defining standard's words, verbatim), `source_url`, `source_page`, `source_clause`, `source_line`, and `ref_id` (provenance only, no foreign key: OD-71), spelled and checked as `base_parameters`' `quantity_kind_*` cells are (migration 156's whitespace and zero-width set). A determination states a figure for disabled people in the units the sources used, converted exactly between them. Three things in that chain are not yet data the pipeline can extend or trust. **A unit can enter only by a hand-written migration** (`base_units` has no writer and no warrant), so a source stating a force in newtons or a luminance in lux has no route in: a hard-coded behaviour (owner, 2026-11-12 (seventh)), and four of the six quantity kinds hold no unit at all. **A quantity kind is warranted by any quote holding a digit**, so "Class 1" or a year warrants "length". And **a determination's bounds are stored as floating-point numbers**: the engine computes them exactly (as fractions) and then writes `float(...)`, so the stored figure is not the figure the sources support (1:12 is stored as 8.333…, not 100/12). A fourth defect, that a determination written under an older rule version reads current, belongs to T-132 (section 4, item 4).
3. **Exact bounds on `specifications` (item 35).** Rebuild `specifications` (create, copy, drop, rename; model on `scripts/migrations/138_drop_medical_lens.sql`, the last rebuild) with `value_min` and `value_max` declared `TEXT`, each NULL or the text `str(fractions.Fraction(…))` prints (an integer, or numerator/denominator in lowest terms with a positive denominator). The CHECK holds the character shape (`typeof = 'text'`, digits with an optional leading `-` and at most one `/`, no `.`); the writer holds lowest terms, and a test round-trips every stored cell through `Fraction`. The copy converts a stored REAL only when it is integral (`value_max = CAST(value_max AS INTEGER)`), as `CAST(CAST(… AS INTEGER) AS TEXT)`; a guard (the `_156_guard` pattern of migration 156) aborts the migration if any stored bound is not integral, because the exact figure of a float cannot be recovered from it and inventing one is a fabricated value. Every view, index, trigger and child foreign key naming the table is recreated (`select type, name from sqlite_master where sql like '%specifications%'`: on 2026-11-19 eight views, two indexes, one trigger, three child tables; four views select `s.*`, so their column types change with the table: read each reader of them). The engine (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`, `_compose_headline`'s return) yields `str(vmin)` and `str(vmax)` for a Fraction instead of `float(...)`, and `STORED_ANSWER`'s comparison in `stale_determinations` then compares text with text; read every other reader of the two columns (`git grep -n -E "value_min|value_max" -- scripts schemas skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'`). Bump `RULE_VERSION` by the engine's own contract in its comment ("same evidence + same rule_version => same answer"): the stored answer changes form for any bound that is not an integer, so give the new label and say so in its comment; the sha payload is unchanged unless you change it (then K01's version sets in `test_db_integrity.py` need the label, as their comments say). Show that the replay plan orders the migration after every data migration (several INSERT these columns: `grep -l -E "value_min|value_max" scripts/migrations/data_*`), with `python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import migrate_db as m;p=m.build_plan();print(p[-1][:2], [s[:2] for s in p if s[0]=='data'][-1])"` (the last step is your schema migration; rule 5).
4. **A rule-version change reads stale (item 33): into T-132, not here.** Append to `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-132-drift-detectors-bind.md`, after its last line, this dated line and nothing else:

   > **Amended 2026-11-19 (third adjudication item 33, ratified 2026-11-19; "you have to compute it", owner 2026-09-09 (evening)):** `stale_determinations` in `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` filters `rule_version = RULE_VERSION`, so a live determination written under an earlier rule reads current. This task also changes it to report such a determination as stale, with `rule_version` among its differing fields, rather than skip it (a cache of a rule no longer in force is not the computation); the Kind line's "no code path" is superseded by this one change. Add a red-then-green case: on a scratch copy, a live determination stamped with an earlier label is reported. The ratchet of item 1 is read after this change.

   Do not change `stale_determinations`' filter in this task.

A new base table `base_unit_spellings` holds each written form of a unit, one per row: `spelling`, `unit_id` (foreign key), the same warrant cells, `judge` and `reason` (non-blank), the stamp; unique on (`spelling`, `unit_id`). So `мм`, `millimetres` and `毫米` are spellings of the one canonical length unit, never second factor-1 units, and `%` may spell a gradient unit and a luminous-reflectance unit at once (two units, two kinds, one spelling). The copy writes each seeded row's text as its unit's first spelling, stamped with the migration's session and no warrant (as seeded: their factors are pinned by T030-13; invent no locator for them). Add `base_unit_spellings: base` to `governance/stage-map.yaml`. Check for a foreign key into `base_units` before the rebuild (`select name from sqlite_master where sql like '%REFERENCES base_units%'` printed none on 2026-11-19).
   - **What reads a spelling:** `dbcore.load_units` (rewritten to join spellings to units) and through it every converter (`unit_kind`, `kind_members`, `canonical_unit`, `to_canonical`, `from_canonical`, `ratio_unit`, `figure_refusal`), the engine's composition, and the shared figure reader below. A `claimed_unit` is matched against every spelling. A spelling that names units of one kind resolves; one that names units of several kinds resolves by the parameter's `quantity_kind` where the caller has it, and otherwise stands alone, with the ambiguity said in the note or the refusal (never a guess, never the first row). No spelling is ambiguous today, so stored answers do not move; prove it (T137-10).
   - **`db.py add-unit`** (`--kind-id`, `--spelling`, `--factor-numerator`, `--factor-denominator`, `--figure-form`, `--system`, `--quote`, `--source-url`, `--source-page` or `--source-clause`, `--source-line`, `--ref-id`, `--judge`, `--reason`, `--session`, `--dry-run`; check every flag name against `dbcore._SECRET_WORDS` first and stop on a clash) writes a unit and its first spelling. Refuses, in order: a blank session; a spelling refused by `dbcore.unit_refusal` or blank; a spelling already spelling a unit of this kind (name it: one written form, one factor, per kind); an unknown kind (name `add-quantity-kind`); a factor that is not two positive integers in lowest terms; a `--figure-form` or `--system` outside its CHECK (`dbcore.check_declared`); a kind's first unit whose factor is not 1, and a second factor-1 unit of a kind (name `add-unit-spelling` for another spelling of it); a missing or partial warrant, a zero-width character, a malformed URL (`_check_base_locator`); a quote with no digit (T-020's floor, digits of any script); and **a quote that does not state the factor**: it holds a valued figure in the new spelling and a valued figure in a held spelling of the same kind whose canonical values are equal under the factor, exactly (Fraction), or, for a kind's first unit, a figure in the new spelling. So `1 in = 25.4 mm` warrants 127/5, `1 in = 25 mm` does not, and `1 in = 25,4 mm` is refused as ambiguous, never read as 4 mm. Name which half was missing.

content.content:
## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

A figure is stated "for" groups of disabled people through lens links, and a determination is computed from the figures in its lens. Five writers still let that record say less than the rulings require. `ALL` (a scope marker the owner removed from the identity lens) is refused only under the `context` basis. A session may record a link as its own judgment (`context`) when the clause it rests on already says so, so a checkable warrant is stored as an uncheckable one. A lens link can be added to or retired from a figure that a live determination was computed from, so the stored determination silently stops matching its evidence. A figure withdrawn as a misreading leaves its pair reading "read in full, nothing found", which is false, and nothing asks for the source to be read again. `set-parameter-kind` is blocked by an open determination gate (a later stage's question ordering a base fact), while `merge-parameter` lets a parameter of one quantity be folded into a parameter of another or of none. `repoint-extraction-relation` points an edge at a withdrawn figure. And "the regulatory stratum" (tiers 4 to 6) is a literal `4` in several places, so a change to the tier ladder would move some readers and not others.

**Evidence commands** (read-only):
**What reads what this task adds:** the refusals: the writers' callers (the run-pipeline skill's steps, research batches). `WITHDRAWN-UNREAD`: `scan_debt.py` (and its `--reread` worklist), `v_reading_owed` (so `defer-reading` and `v_deferred_acts`), `cell-status`. `dbcore.REGULATORY_FROM_TIER`: every tier comparison named above. **Without this task**, a determination can stand on a lens its evidence no longer has; a group is stated "for everyone" by a marker the owner removed; a misread figure's source reads as examined and empty; a merged parameter's figures sit under another quantity; and a change to the tier ladder moves some readers and not others.

**Not in this task (plan edits the coordinator makes, adjudication section 4 item 13):** the T-078, T-083 and T-109 file amendments. Not here either: T-056's engine, the `add-conflict` refusal, the `context` tier floor's exception for a clause naming no one (OD-47's follow-on).

**Migration discipline (item 4).** Apply only with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py`; prove with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"` (exit 0) and `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep` (PASS). No `data_*` file. Then `python3 scripts/generate/context_map.py` and include `governance/context-map.yaml` if it changed.

**Code size.** Report `git diff --shortstat "$BASE_PRE" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` (after `git add`); name what each addition reads and what it replaces (the literal `4`s, the gate branch of `set-parameter-kind`).

## 5. Caller sweep
**Callers found on 2026-11-19** (each in scope; re-run): `scripts/db.py` (the functions named in section 4, `cell_status` and its docstring at the ledger precedence list, `_parameter_row`); `scripts/dbcore.py`; `scripts/audit/scan_debt.py`, `scripts/audit/code_value_identity_audit.py`, `scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py`, and the other readers of `v_scan_ledger` (`scripts/audit/verified_scan_integrity.py`, `scripts/audit/skill_vocabulary_audit.py`: read whether they list statuses); views `v_scan_ledger`, `v_reading_owed` (and `v_deferred_acts`, which reads it, and `source_scans`, whose DDL comment names the ledger: mentions unless a sentence changes); tests `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py` (T-126 cases accepting `ALL` under `named_in_text` or `heading`, T-083's `T083-04` asserting the gate refusal, the test reading `db._REGULATORY_FROM_TIER`), `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py` (the cases enumerating ledger statuses, and `cell-status` bucket sums), `scripts/tests/test_scan_contract.py` (ledger status cases); skills `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md` (ledger statuses, the lens bases, `set-parameter-kind`); prose `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` (ledger and stratum sentences), `governance/context-map.yaml` (regenerated). A test that asserted a refusal this task removes (the gate on a kind) is a caller updated to the ruled behaviour, named in the commit body.
**Step 2: red before, green after, one group per item.** Case ids `T138-NN` (`git grep -c '"T138-' -- scripts/tests` printed nothing on 2026-11-19), in `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py` beside the T-126 and T-078 cases (items 1 to 6) and in the same file for item 7. A live determination is built as the G04 fixture of that file builds one (it un-retires a determination on the test's scratch copy; derive it by query); a retired figure, a full reading and a later reading are built with the writers on the scratch copy, labelled `TASK-FIXTURE`. Never type an id, code, tier or count the database can derive. Show each case red on a seeded defect you then remove (restore byte for byte; `cmp`).
**Step 3, after the change: the after-run.** The same loop with `after-`; compare check by check: `diff <(grep -E '\[✗\]|^ *FAIL|^FAILED|VERDICT: FAIL' "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt") <(grep -E '\[✗\]|^ *FAIL|^FAILED|VERDICT: FAIL' "$SCRATCH/after-$c.txt")`. No failing case may appear that was not failing before, except a case asserting a behaviour this task changes by ruling, updated and named.
